hook.text: Hotels track how fast rooms are booking compared to the same period last year. This 'booking pace' reveals demand early.

buildup.text: If bookings are running 20% ahead of last year for a given date, it signals high demand—time to raise prices.

discovery.text: Conversely, if pace is lagging, revenue managers might lower rates, add promotions, or alert sales teams to fill the gap.

twist.text: Booking pace can be misleading. A convention might book a block early, inflating pace, then cancel later—a false signal.

climax.text: Revenue managers check pace daily—sometimes hourly. It's the pulse of the hotel's financial health for any future date.

punchline.text: How fast rooms sell tells you what to charge next. Pace drives price.

quiz.question: What does 'booking pace' measure?
options: How quickly rooms are being reserved compared to the same period last year
